If it's under your shoulder blades(scapula), you need to look for the muscle antagonist and strengthen that first. Without seeing you in person, it would be hard for me to gauge, but I would assume you could start with your pecs.

Try massagenerd.com - the site is a little wonky on the layout, but the info there is pretty spot on.

Also, the tennis ball things - get yourself a regular sock (no ankle sock). Put two tennis balls in, and push them alllll the way down to the toe. The second ball should end by the bottom of the ankle. Now tie a knot to hold the tennis balls in place. They should be touching.

Lay out on the ground, and then line the tennis balls so they go on either side of your spine. Now roll on your back making the tennis balls roll up and down your spine(they should be hugging around it, you are aiming for the muscles in the lamina groove).

You can do this from the top of your shoulders to where your closing ribs start. I wouldn't put too much pressure on those little guys because you could break them free. But around your shoulder blades? Go to town!
